subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared filename decoder live, and how much channel migration is required before this issue can close?
rationale: Root policy keeps core lean and plugin-safe; current code has separate core and Feishu parsers, and the open candidate PR is partial, so automation should not choose the permanent API boundary alone.

options.title: Media-core shared helper
options.body: Put the decoder in a plugin-safe media-core or SDK-exposed boundary, then migrate remote media and the proven Feishu filename paths through it before closing this issue.

options.title: Narrow Feishu-only path
options.body: Keep the current Feishu-local recovery and close only narrower Feishu bugs, leaving this broader shared decoder request open or explicitly deferred.

options.title: Defer broad migration
options.body: Treat multi-channel decoder work as lower priority until another non-Feishu channel reproduces filename corruption with concrete evidence.

recommendation.title: Media-core shared helper
recommendation.body: Put the decoder in a plugin-safe media-core or SDK-exposed boundary, then migrate remote media and the proven Feishu filename paths through it before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about the media-core/src/media ownership boundary, and @steipete authored the current remote-media consolidation path.
